title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Non-executive directors, the CEO and the Company Secretary of Endeavour; Executive Committee members and their direct reports; and any other team member or person (including support personnel) nominated by the Board Chair, CEO or Company Secretary as likely to have access to Inside Information from time to time. Subject to Trading Windows, dealing clearance, the collateral ban, the six month rule and the flat hedging ban.

tiers.name: Endeavour directors
tiers.description: Directors of Endeavour, including the CEO and the Board Chair. Designated Persons whose dealings are endorsed by the CLO and Company Secretary and approved by the Board Chair (or, for the Board Chair, the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee Chair), and who must seek confirmation from the Company Secretary before relying on an Excluded Dealing.

tiers.name: Executive Committee member
tiers.description: An executive who reports directly to the CEO and is part of the Group Executive Leadership Team of Endeavour, except the CEO. A Designated Person, endorsed by the CLO and Company Secretary and approved by the CEO; their direct reports are also Designated Persons, approved by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Endeavour equity-based remuneration plan participants
tiers.description: Participants in any Endeavour Board approved plan under which an employee is provided with Endeavour Securities as part of at-risk variable or discretionary remuneration, including short-term, long-term, recognition and retention plans, but not general employee equity plans. Subject to the paragraph 9 hedging ban over unvested plan securities and vested plan securities subject to a dealing restriction.

tiers.name: team members
tiers.description: A director, officer or employee (full time, part time or casual) of Endeavour Group, or a contractor or consultant whose engagement terms apply the policy. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the market perception obligation and confidentiality, but not by Trading Windows, clearance, the collateral ban, the six month rule or the general hedging ban unless also a Designated Person or plan participant.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A closely connected person or entity to a Designated Person or equity plan participant: spouse, domestic partner or dependent child (including dependent adult or step-child); a relative residing with them; another family member they may be expected to influence or be influenced by in relation to dealings in securities; a company, trust, partnership or other entity they or those persons control or significantly influence; and the trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement of which they or those persons are a beneficiary. The Designated Person must do on the Associate's behalf any act the policy requires of the Associate.

definitions.hedging_definition: The use of securities to offset the risk of adverse price movement in securities or entering into a transaction designed to limited exposure to economic risk in securities.

windows.start_anchor: first trading day after Endeavour's half-year results are released to ASX
first trading day after Endeavour's full-year results are released to ASX
first trading day after Endeavour's Annual General Meeting
lodgement with ASIC of a prospectus, cleansing notice or similar disclosure document
windows.end_anchor: while that document remains open for acceptances

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The policy is window-based rather than blackout-based, so any period that is not a Trading Window is a closed period. The Board may determine additional Trading Window periods, and the Board Chair may determine variations to any of the window periods on the recommendation of the Chief Legal Officer and Company Secretary. Windows are effective only when notified: the opening of Trading Windows will be notified to Designated Persons by email and Designated Persons must not assume a Trading Window is open in the absence of such notification.

rules.detail: A flat prohibition on Designated Persons and their Associates entering into Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, not just plan securities and regardless of vesting. Hedging arrangement is defined by economic effect, capturing any transaction designed to limit exposure to economic risk in securities. Paragraph 16 provides an exemption route only for dealing outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances and for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b (collateral), not for 11d, so there is no approval pathway for hedging.
rules.evidence: Additionally, Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).

rules.detail: Non-executive directors and the CEO are Designated Persons, so the flat 11d hedging ban applies to them and to their Associates over any Endeavour Securities, including shares acquired on market outside any plan. No exemption route exists: paragraph 16 reaches only trading window exemptions and prohibited dealings under 11b.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are: non-executive directors, the CEO and the Company Secretary of Endeavour ... Additionally, Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities

rules.detail: Executive Committee members and their direct reports are Designated Persons and are therefore subject to the same flat prohibition on Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, with no approval pathway.
rules.evidence: Executives Committee members and their direct reports; ... Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities

rules.detail: The 11d hedging ban applies directly to Associates of Designated Persons, and the Designated Person is responsible for making them aware of it and taking reasonable steps to ensure compliance, so a collar cannot be routed through a spouse, controlled entity or trust.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).

rules.detail: Plan participants and their Associates must not hedge unvested Endeavour Securities allocated under an equity-based remuneration plan. This applies to every participant, whether or not they are a Designated Person.
rules.evidence: If you participate in an Endeavour equity-based remuneration plan you (or your Associate) must not enter into any Hedging arrangement in respect to any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

rules.detail: The paragraph 9 ban expressly extends to vested plan securities that remain subject to a dealing restriction, so a holding lock keeps the shares out of reach of any collar.
rules.evidence: must not enter into any Hedging arrangement in respect to any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

rules.detail: Paragraph 9 stops at vested securities that are free of any dealing restriction, so a plan participant who is not a Designated Person may hedge vested unrestricted plan shares, subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the market perception obligation.
rules.evidence: any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

rules.detail: A team member who is neither a Designated Person nor an equity plan participant is not caught by either hedging prohibition; only the insider trading prohibition and the market perception obligation apply, and there is no Trading Window or clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: There are additional obligations which apply to Designated Persons and their Associates and to participants in Endeavour's equity-based remuneration plans.

rules.detail: The definition of derivative expressly names collars, together with options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and contracts for difference, and defines them by their function of limiting the economic risk of holding securities. A purchased put plus written call over Endeavour shares is therefore a Hedging arrangement banned by 11d for Designated Persons and their Associates, with no venue limitation and no approval route.
rules.evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Endeavour Securities are treated identically; in addition paragraph 11c separately bans dealing in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities within a six month period.
rules.evidence: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain).

rules.detail: The derivative and hedging restrictions in paragraph 11 apply only to Designated Persons and their Associates, and paragraph 9 only to equity plan participants, so an ordinary team member dealing in derivatives over their own vested unrestricted shares is not restricted by this policy.
rules.evidence: There are obligations in this policy that apply to Endeavour Group and to all team members. There are additional obligations which apply to Designated Persons and their Associates and to participants in Endeavour's equity-based remuneration plans.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure is a forward contract and a transaction that operates to limit economic risk, so it is a Hedging arrangement prohibited by 11d. If it also uses Endeavour Securities as collateral it engages the 11b collateral ban, for which an approval route does exist under paragraph 16b.
rules.evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. A short sale by a Designated Person would still be a dealing requiring a Trading Window and clearance, would engage the six month rule, and a synthetic short would be caught by the hedging ban.

Stock lending is expressly within the definition of deal, so it is not prohibited as such but must occur inside a Trading Window with written clearance from the relevant approver, executed within three business days. There is no separate stock lending prohibition.
rules.evidence: Deal includes to: ... margin lend, stock lend or make other financing arrangements for securities

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are expressly named in the definition of derivative, which is framed as a product or transaction operating to limit economic risk, so CFDs over Endeavour Securities are Hedging arrangements banned by 11d, and are separately caught by the six month rule in 11c.
rules.evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending using Endeavour Securities as collateral is a prohibited dealing under 11b, but the December 2022 revision added an express clearance process: under 16b a Designated Person or Associate may seek approval for a prohibited dealing under 11b, submitting written details of the securitisation arrangement concurrently to the CLO and Company Secretary as endorsers and the Board Chair and the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee as approvers, who may grant, refuse or make it conditional in absolute discretion without reasons.
rules.evidence: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy

rules.detail: Paragraph 11 applies only to Designated Persons and their Associates; the policy is silent on margin lending by other team members.

Using Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction is expressly prohibited unless otherwise permitted under the policy, and paragraph 16b supplies that permission route. The ban is drafted at the level of collateral use in any financial transaction, so it captures a charge, mortgage or pledge over the shares however the financing is characterised. Making financing arrangements for securities is also itself a dealing.
rules.evidence: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy

rules.detail: The collateral prohibition extends beyond margin loans to any financial transaction in which Endeavour Securities are used as collateral, so the loan leg of a funded collar is squarely within it. Unusually the policy provides a dedicated approval process for exactly this, requiring written details of the securitisation arrangement, dual endorsement and dual approval at Board Chair and ARCMC Chair level.
rules.evidence: an approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 16b then you must provide written details of the securitisation arrangement and any other information requested by Endeavour.

rules.detail: The collateral ban and its clearance process sit within the Designated Persons obligations and do not reach other team members.

A six month buy/sell window applying both to the same Endeavour Securities and to derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities. The only carve-out is the exercise of rights under an equity-based remuneration plan and the subsequent dealing of those securities in accordance with the policy.
rules.evidence: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain). This does not prohibit the exercise of rights under an Endeavour equity-based remuneration plan and the subsequent dealing of those securities in accordance with this policy

clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than the next business day after the dealing is finalised
clearance.evidence: A request may be granted, refused or made conditional at the absolute discretion of the approver and without providing any reasons. A refusal is final and binding on the person making the request and must be kept confidential. ... the Designated Person or Associate must undertake the dealing within three business days of obtaining the clearance (unless clearance is revoked by the approver).

clearance.post_trade_to: the approver and the Company Secretary; directors must also comply with the requirements to notify directors' interests to the relevant authorities, and must seek confirmation from the Company Secretary before relying on an Excluded Dealing
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than the next business day after the dealing is finalised
clearance.evidence: Endeavour directors must seek confirmation from the Company Secretary before dealing in Endeavour Securities in reliance of an Excluded Dealing.

clearance.approver: CEO, on the endorsement of the CLO & Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: the approver and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than the next business day after the dealing is finalised
clearance.evidence: Executive Committee member (except CEO & CLO) and Associates | CLO & Company Secretary | CEO

clearance.approver: The approver of the associated Designated Person; the Designated Person must obtain the clearance on the Associate's behalf

clearance.evidence: Where the policy requires an act from an Associate (such as obtaining an approval), the Designated Person must do that act on behalf of their Associate.

acquiring Endeavour Securities under a share purchase plan or rights issue made available to all or most of Endeavour shareholders

exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship where the disposal of Endeavour Securities is the only practical method of overcoming the hardship ... A liability to pay tax does not normally constitute severe financial difficulty.
a requirement under a court order or court enforceable undertaking

exemption_authority: The Board is the policy's Exception Authority. Operationally, paragraph 16 allows a Designated Person or Associate to request either a trading window exemption to deal outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances, or approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b (use of Endeavour Securities as collateral), the latter decided by the Board Chair and the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee on the endorsement of the CLO and Company Secretary. Neither route is available where there would be a breach of the insider trading prohibition or market perception obligation, and neither extends to the paragraph 11d hedging prohibition or the paragraph 11c six month rule.
jurisdiction_overlays: Paragraph 4: the insider trading prohibition applies to acts in Australia as well as outside Australia

bespoke_clauses.topic: collars named in the derivative definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: derivative: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names collars specifically and defines derivatives by economic function, so there is no argument that a put plus call structure falls outside the hedging prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.topic: flat hedging ban for Designated Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Associates must not ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to plan securities or to unvested holdings, so a Designated Person cannot collar even shares bought on market with their own money, and paragraph 16 offers no exemption route for it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person or their Associate may request to ... seek an approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b ... you must provide written details of the securitisation arrangement and any other information requested by Endeavour. The request should be submitted concurrently to the CLO and Company Secretary (Endorsers) and the Chair and the Board Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee (Approvers).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Endeavour is one of the few ASX policies with an express pathway to approve pledging shares as loan collateral, so the financing leg of a funded structure is negotiable at Board Chair level even though the hedging leg is not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is drafted at the level of collateral in any financial transaction, so it catches any bank facility secured on the shares regardless of how the loan is documented, and approval must be obtained before the security is granted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a permitted derivative programme could not be entered, rolled or unwound within six months, so short-dated or frequently rolled collars are unavailable to Designated Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The opening of Trading Windows will be notified to Designated Persons by email. Designated Persons must not assume that a Trading Window is open in the absence of such notification.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Windows are not self-executing from the results calendar; the bank should require evidence of the notification email before scheduling execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Designated Person or Associate must undertake the dealing within three business days of obtaining the clearance ... A dealing must be placed within a Trading Window (not prior) and executed by 4.00pm on the last day of the relevant Trading Window. A dealing may settle after the close of the Trading Window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved leg must be placed and executed inside the window and within three business days of clearance, though settlement may fall outside, which is helpful for a structure with a delayed settlement date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal includes to: ... margin lend, stock lend or make other financing arrangements for securities; ... transfer ownership between accounts, brokers or sponsors.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a custody or collateral account, and the financing arrangement itself, are each dealings needing a Trading Window and clearance, not just administrative steps.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates ... includes ... a company, trust, partnership or other entity that the Relevant Person, or any of the persons mentioned above, control or significantly influence; or the trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangements of which the Relevant Person ... is a beneficiary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a family trust, controlled company or the trustee of a fund in which the executive is a beneficiary does not escape the hedging ban or the collateral clearance requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not deal in Endeavour Securities (or securities of another company) if the proposed dealing could be perceived by the market as you taking advantage of your position in an inappropriate way.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An independent, self-executing obligation that applies to every team member at all times and cannot be waived by any exemption, so even an approved collateral arrangement remains vulnerable to a perception challenge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A liability to pay tax does not normally constitute severe financial difficulty.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Funding a tax bill on vesting is expressly not an exceptional circumstance, closing off the most common justification for an out-of-window monetisation.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for an Endeavour Designated Person, and the obstacle is the hedging leg rather than the financing leg. Paragraph 11d prohibits Designated Persons and their Associates from entering into Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, vested or not and however acquired, and the definitions put the point beyond argument by defining derivative to include collars and by defining a Hedging arrangement as any transaction designed to limit exposure to economic risk in securities. Paragraph 16 provides exemption routes only for dealing outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances and for the paragraph 11b collateral prohibition, so there is no approval pathway for hedging, and paragraph 11c would independently bar entering and unwinding derivative positions within six months. The financing leg, by contrast, is expressly negotiable: the December 2022 revision added a clearance process under which a Designated Person may seek approval to use Endeavour Securities as collateral in a financial transaction, supported by written details of the securitisation arrangement, endorsed by the CLO and Company Secretary and approved by the Board Chair and the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee. Only an equity plan participant who is not a Designated Person retains room to hedge, and then only over vested plan securities that are free of any dealing restriction.
